correctness.rationale: Direct block multiplication gives X²=0 iff AB=0. Fixed rank i of A yields R_q(a,b,i) choices, fixed rank j of B inside ker A yields R_q(b-i,c,j), and rank X=i+j+rank(ker B→F_q^a/im A). The restriction/quotient map on C is surjective with kernel dimension ac-(a-i)(c-j), proving every multiplicity for all finite fields; matrix-rank count R_q is the standard Gaussian formula including zero dimensions. A matching in the complete tripartite support pattern yields all ranks to min(floor(N/2),N-maxpart), while square zero and block supports provide the exact upper bound. An independent one-sum ungraded count checks normalization; 41 complete finite field enumerations test small cases. The computations are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: No matching finite-field rank distribution for square-zero matrices in a prescribed three-block parabolic radical was identified after targeted statement-level comparisons. Kirillov/Ekhad–Zeilberger count full upper triangular square-zero matrices (including a rank-refined recurrence); Boos classifies complex parabolic orbits without finite-field rank multiplicities; geometric varieties-of-complexes results concern the two adjacent maps; and Nien counts character degrees of the associated unipotent group. None implies the displayed three-block restriction with total matrix-rank fibers without additional enumeration. An equivalent indexed differently remains possible.
residual_risks: Boos 2012 complex parabolic orbit classification could potentially be converted into the exact finite-field rank counts through additional rational orbit-size calculations; such an equivalent enumerative corollary was not found.
Prior literature on nilpotent order-two orbits in parabolic radicals may encode the same finite-field polynomial under orbit parameters not returned by searches.

Full text of Nien 2021 and the earlier De Concini–Strickland varieties-of-complexes paper was not inspected; available descriptions suggest different invariants, but cannot exclude hidden equivalent formulas.

value.rationale: This is a complete q- and block-size-uniform arithmetic classification of a natural square-zero locus in the nilradical of a parabolic matrix algebra, refined by a conjugacy-invariant operator rank. The unrestricted long block creates nontrivial residual-rank fibers invisible from the rank vectors of the adjacent complex; the matching threshold gives a sharp structural support theorem. It extends beyond isolated numerics and has a plausible use for finite parabolic radical distributions and degeneration comparisons. Its value does not rely on asserting an independent-audit outcome or a generalization beyond three blocks.
